devotionFirstRites.name: First Rites
devotionFirstRites.flavor: Before the temple a stone, and before the stone a promise.
devotionFirstRites.text: Shrines cost 25% less production and give +2 faith.

pastoralShrines.name: Pastoral Shrines
pastoralShrines.flavor: The herd is counted twice: once by the herdsman, once by the god.
pastoralShrines.text: Worked pastures gain +1 faith and +1 food. Your capital gains +2 production while you control an improved pasture.
pastoralShrines.note: Not built, both halves together: the law can dress a herder's ground, and nothing can yet ask whether the realm keeps a single pen anywhere at all, which is the clause the capital's hammers hang on.
deferred: worked pastures pay an offering of faith and a little more food
your capital works harder while you keep a penned herd anywhere at all

layOfferings.name: Lay Offerings
layOfferings.flavor: The miners leave a little of what they cut on the ledge outside.
layOfferings.text: Worked mines and camps gain +1 faith. A city working at least two gains +3 gold, once per city.

theMonasticTable.name: The Monastic Table
theMonasticTable.flavor: The kitchen is a kind of prayer, and it is answered.
theMonasticTable.text: Cities keeping a rite gain +2 food and +2 production.

theVotiveFields.name: The Votive Fields
theVotiveFields.flavor: The field is the first altar and the harvest the first hymn.
theVotiveFields.text: Worked farms and plantations in cities keeping a rite gain +1 food and +1 faith.

theOmenSchools.name: The Omen Schools
theOmenSchools.flavor: Read the sky long enough and it begins to read back.
theOmenSchools.text: Cities keeping a rite gain +2 science and +1 culture.

hearthBlessings.name: Hearth Blessings
hearthBlessings.flavor: A house that has never been this full does not know how to be quiet.
hearthBlessings.text: Natural growth to a city's new population high grants 8 faith. A Shrine there also grants 8 food.
hearthBlessings.note: Not built: a town remembers how many people live in it and not how many ever did, so nothing can tell a new high from an ordinary birth.
deferred: a town growing past the largest it has ever been gives thanks in faith
a shrine there sets bread on the table besides

ritesOfLabor.name: Rites of Labor
ritesOfLabor.flavor: Worship with the sleeves rolled up.
ritesOfLabor.text: Cities keeping a rite gain +20% production toward buildings and +2 gold.

theBookOfMercy.name: The Book of Mercy
theBookOfMercy.flavor: Two pages: one for the grief, one for the watch kept over it.
theBookOfMercy.text: Once drafted, unlock the Rites of Mourning and the Watch after Divination. No chair required.
theBookOfMercy.note: Not built: neither observance has been written into the book of rites, so the charter has nothing to open. The row is kept so the two may be written.
deferred: a town may mourn, and while it grieves its people ask far less of it and it raises no soldiers
a town may keep a watch, seeing the raiders' camps around it and taking faith for every kill near its walls

theRitesCommonwealth.name: The Rites Commonwealth
theRitesCommonwealth.flavor: A realm at prayer together, and one village that is not.
theRitesCommonwealth.text: Cities keeping a rite gain +3 production and demand 15% less population happiness. Your cities without a rite gain −1 happiness.

pilgrimsWelcome.name: Pilgrims' Welcome
pilgrimsWelcome.flavor: Whoever they had come to pray to, they came hungry.
pilgrimsWelcome.text: Cities with a Shrine following any religion gain +2 food and +2 gold. You need not have founded it.
pilgrimsWelcome.note: Not built: the law can ask whether a town keeps your faith and cannot yet ask whether it keeps somebody's.
deferred: towns with a shrine that keep any faith at all, yours or a rival's, eat better and trade better

monasticCopyists.name: Monastic Copyists
monasticCopyists.flavor: Two rooms, one lamp, and the whole of what anyone remembers.
monasticCopyists.text: Cities with a Temple and Library gain +3 science and +3 culture.

theHealing.name: The Healing
theHealing.flavor: They walked in leaning on each other and walked out leaning on nothing.
theHealing.text: Spend faith in an owned city to heal your units in and beside it by up to 30 health each. Once per city and affected unit per turn; price depends on actual healing.
theHealing.note: Not built: there is no order a town can give that spends faith on the wounded, and no price quoted for one.
deferred: a town may spend faith to mend your soldiers standing in it and beside it

theLoaves.name: The Loaves
theLoaves.flavor: The basket went down the whole table and came back with something in it.
theLoaves.text: Spend faith to add one citizen to an owned city, once per turn. Price follows remaining growth cost, minimum 80 faith; no natural-growth rewards or retained food.
theLoaves.note: Not built: there is no order a town can give that buys a citizen, and no price quoted for one.
deferred: a town may spend faith to seat another citizen at once

theFeastDays.name: The Feast Days
theFeastDays.flavor: Twelve quiet years, and then the whole street eats in it.
theFeastDays.text: Every twelve turns a city keeps a rite while this is seated, gain faith equal to its population and +2 happiness there for five turns.
theFeastDays.note: Not built: nothing counts the years a particular town has spent keeping its rites while this law stood.
deferred: a town that has kept its rites long enough holds a feast, takes faith for every citizen at it, and is glad of it for a while

devotionTheQuietHours.name: The Quiet Hours
devotionTheQuietHours.flavor: Say it slower. There is more of the evening than you think.
devotionTheQuietHours.text: Rites granted while this is seated last five turns longer.
devotionTheQuietHours.note: Not built: a law may make the realm's rites run longer by a share of their length and cannot yet add a flat count of turns to them.
deferred: a rite granted while this stands runs five turns longer than it would

theRitesCharter.name: The Rites Charter
theRitesCharter.flavor: A small roof, a short road, and a blessing for the men who take it.
theRitesCharter.text: Once drafted, unlock the Chapel for construction under its normal site rules, and the Rite of Passage after Bronze Working. No chair required.
theRitesCharter.note: Not built, both halves together: the chapel is ready to be opened and the rite charted beside it has not been written into the book of rites.
deferred: the chapel may be raised in your towns under its ordinary rules
a town may keep the Rite of Passage, and the soldiers raised there are hardier for the rest of their lives

theLivingHymnal.name: The Living Hymnal
theLivingHymnal.flavor: Every verse was somebody's first morning in the faith.
theLivingHymnal.text: While active, gains +2 science and +2 culture per turn in your capital for each foreign city first converted to your religion, at most +24 of each.
theLivingHymnal.note: Not built: nothing keeps a record of which foreign towns your faith reached first, and a record that could be made twice would pay twice.
deferred: your capital learns and sings a little more for every foreign town you were the first to bring to your faith, up to a limit

missionaryHospitality.name: Missionary Hospitality
missionaryHospitality.flavor: Send them out fed. They will be a long time coming back.
missionaryHospitality.text: Religious units cost 15% less faith. Your first conversion of each foreign city grants 20 food in your capital and 20 culture.
missionaryHospitality.note: Not built, both halves together: nothing marks the first time a foreign town turns to your faith, and the roster has no word that gathers the prophet, the apostle and the inquisitor into one line.
deferred: clergy cost less faith to call
the first time each foreign town turns to your faith your capital is fed and the realm sings

theAlmsRoads.name: The Alms Roads
theAlmsRoads.flavor: The road out of a temple town is never empty and never only cargo.
theAlmsRoads.text: Domestic routes from Temple cities give their destination +3 food and +2 gold. Your foreign routes from Temple cities give you +3 faith and +2 gold, and the host +1 gold.
theAlmsRoads.note: Not built: a caravan carries no faith, and a law of yours cannot put coin in another empire's purse.
deferred: roads from your temple towns feed and enrich the towns they reach
roads from them into another realm pay you in faith and coin, and pay your host a little too

consecratedLabor.name: Consecrated Labor
consecratedLabor.flavor: The spade was blessed on a Tuesday and has not stopped since.
consecratedLabor.text: Workers may be purchased with faith in Temple cities at their normal equivalent purchase price. Those purchased workers gain +1 charge on creation.
consecratedLabor.note: Not built: the faith bank sells clergy and houses of learning, and nothing opens it to the spade.
deferred: workers may be bought with faith in temple towns at the price coin would have paid
and those workers come with an extra charge in them

theVotiveCompanies.name: The Votive Companies
theVotiveCompanies.flavor: They took the vow and the spear in the same afternoon.
theVotiveCompanies.text: Temple cities keeping a rite may purchase military units with faith at their normal equivalent purchase price. All your military units cost +1 gold upkeep while this is seated.
theVotiveCompanies.note: Not built, both halves together: the faith bank does not sell soldiers, and the price the other half charges is no card on its own.
deferred: temple towns keeping a rite may buy soldiers with faith at the price coin would have paid
and every soldier you keep costs a coin more while this stands

theConcord.name: The Concord
theConcord.flavor: Three at the hearth are a household. The rest are a crowd.
theConcord.text: In each city following any religion, the first three citizens demand no population happiness.
theConcord.note: Not built: the waiver on a town's first citizens is a rule of the whole realm and cannot yet be narrowed to the towns that keep a faith.
deferred: in a town that keeps any faith the first three citizens ask nothing of the realm's contentment

theParishRolls.name: The Parish Rolls
theParishRolls.flavor: The priest already knew every name. The clerk only wrote them down.
theParishRolls.text: Cities with a Temple following any religion cost one less authority, minimum one.
theParishRolls.note: Not built: the writ is granted to the realm as capacity and is never taken off a particular town's price.
deferred: a temple town that keeps any faith is cheaper to hold, though never free

devotionTheSaintsFields.name: The Saints' Fields
devotionTheSaintsFields.flavor: They buried him at the edge of the barley and the barley never forgot.
devotionTheSaintsFields.text: Worked Holy Sites give +3 food and +3 production. A city working one gains +2 happiness, once per city.

theCathedralWorks.name: The Cathedral Works
theCathedralWorks.flavor: Three generations of masons and one drawing.
theCathedralWorks.text: Gain +30% production toward Cathedrals. Cities with one gain +5 production and +5 science.

sainthood.name: Sainthood
sainthood.flavor: He did one ordinary thing very well and they kept the hand.
sainthood.text: Spending a great person by act or work in an owned Temple city's territory leaves a relic in that city if it has none.
sainthood.note: Not built: nothing can set a relic down but the apostle who carries one.
deferred: spending a great person in a temple town's country leaves a relic behind in that town if it has none

thePilgrimRoad.name: The Pilgrim Road
thePilgrimRoad.flavor: The inns along it were built by people who were only passing through.
thePilgrimRoad.text: Your routes ending at a city holding a relic or working a Holy Site grant +2 faith to both operator and host, once each. Domestic routes grant +2 total.
thePilgrimRoad.note: Not built: a caravan carries no faith, and a law of yours cannot pay another empire.
deferred: your roads ending at a town that holds a relic or works a holy site pay faith to the sender and to the host alike

theSpiritualHost.name: The Spiritual Host
theSpiritualHost.flavor: An army that knows what it is for marches shorter days and farther.
theSpiritualHost.text: Your military units gain +4 strength in territory following your religion. Temple cities gain +2 happiness while you are at war.

theCongregationRolls.name: The Congregation Rolls
theCongregationRolls.flavor: Every name on the roll is a hand somewhere else.
theCongregationRolls.text: Each foreign city following your religion gives your capital +2 gold and +2 science, at most +24 of each.

theSecondProphet.name: The Second Prophet
theSecondProphet.flavor: One voice was never going to be enough.
theSecondProphet.text: Prophets purchased while this is seated begin with one additional charge. Existing faith prices and charge costs remain.

missionHouses.name: Mission Houses
missionHouses.flavor: A bed, a map and a door that opens the right way.
missionHouses.text: Your proclamations apply 30% more pressure. Religious units gain +1 movement.
missionHouses.note: Not built, both halves together: a proclamation's weight can be shifted by a flat figure and not by a share of itself, and the roster has no word that gathers the prophet, the apostle and the inquisitor into one line.
deferred: your proclamations press harder on the towns that hear them
clergy travel farther in a turn

theFestivalCalendar.name: The Festival Calendar
theFestivalCalendar.flavor: Mark the days first. The year arranges itself around them.
theFestivalCalendar.text: Cities keeping a rite gain +20% food and +20% culture.

consecratedGround.name: Consecrated Ground
consecratedGround.flavor: They paid for the meadow in candles.
consecratedGround.text: Purchase legal city tiles with faith instead of gold at the same quoted price. Normal range and purchase limits apply.
consecratedGround.note: Not built: land is bought out of the treasury and nothing opens the faith bank to it.
deferred: hexes may be bought with faith at the price coin would have paid

theCouncil.name: The Council
theCouncil.flavor: They argued for a season and changed one sentence.
theCouncil.text: Once per research age, spend a Prophet's two charges in your original holy city to replace one follower belief, choosing from three eligible alternatives. You must still control the faith's original seat.
theCouncil.note: Not built: there is no council a prophet can call, and no offer of beliefs to lay before one.
deferred: once an age a prophet at your faith's first seat may set one follower belief aside and choose another from three

theSettledFaith.name: The Settled Faith
theSettledFaith.flavor: A faith that has stopped travelling has time to read.
theSettledFaith.text: Temple cities keeping a rite gain +20% science and +2 happiness. Your proclamations apply 25% less pressure.
theSettledFaith.note: Not built, both halves together: a proclamation's weight can be shifted by a flat figure and not by a share of itself.
deferred: temple towns keeping a rite learn faster and are gladder
and your proclamations press more gently for it

theConsecratedWorkshops.name: The Consecrated Workshops
theConsecratedWorkshops.flavor: The saints are carved by the hands that cut the roof beams.
theConsecratedWorkshops.text: Cities keeping a rite gain +20% production. Their Cathedrals give an additional +4 production.

pilgrimHospices.name: Pilgrim Hospices
pilgrimHospices.flavor: Beds enough for the road, and a bell for the ones who stay.
pilgrimHospices.text: Cities of at least ten population with a Cathedral following any religion gain +20% food and +3 happiness.
pilgrimHospices.note: Not built: the law can ask whether a town keeps your faith and cannot yet ask whether it keeps somebody's.
deferred: great towns with a cathedral that keep any faith eat well and are glad of it

theHolyInquisition.name: The Holy Inquisition
theHolyInquisition.flavor: A quiet office, a long memory, and a very short list.
theHolyInquisition.text: Rival pressure entering your cities is reduced by 40%, multiplying existing defences. Inquisitors cost 25% less faith.
theHolyInquisition.note: Not built, both halves together: a town's resistance to another faith belongs to its temple and cannot yet be raised for the realm at large.
deferred: a rival's faith presses far more weakly on your towns, over whatever defence they already keep
inquisitors cost less faith to call

theHolyArmy.name: The Holy Army
theHolyArmy.flavor: The relic goes at the head of the column and the column keeps up.
theHolyArmy.text: Your military units gain +5 strength in territory following your religion. Cities holding a relic train military units 30% faster.

theSacredTreasury.name: The Sacred Treasury
theSacredTreasury.flavor: Gold, bone and barley, kept in the same cold room.
theSacredTreasury.text: A city with a Cathedral, a relic and a worked Holy Site gains +20% gold and culture, and +25% production toward wonders and the Magnum Opus. Pays once per city.
theSacredTreasury.note: Not built: a bonus on building can name one row or one category, never a marvel and the last work of all at once.
deferred: a town with a cathedral, a relic and a worked holy site grows rich, sings, and builds the great works faster

theBishopsChoice.name: The Bishop's Choice
theBishopsChoice.flavor: He read the three names twice and chose the one he already meant to.
theBishopsChoice.text: When you complete a Cathedral, choose its consecration from the legal set instead of receiving a random one.
theBishopsChoice.note: Not built: a cathedral's consecration is settled as the roof goes on and there is no offer to put before anyone.
deferred: when you finish a cathedral you choose its consecration instead of being given one

theGreatConsecration.name: The Great Consecration
theGreatConsecration.flavor: The whole world, kneeling in the same direction.
theGreatConsecration.text: Each foreign city following your religion grants +5% production toward the Magnum Opus, at most +40%.
theGreatConsecration.note: Not built: the hammers behind a thing are raised by a flat share and cannot yet be counted out of a congregation.
deferred: every foreign town that keeps your faith puts a little more behind the Magnum Opus, up to a limit

theCloisteredRealm.name: The Cloistered Realm
theCloisteredRealm.flavor: The gate is shut, the library is open, and nobody is shouting.
theCloisteredRealm.text: Cities with a Cathedral keeping a rite gain +25% science and +25% production. Your proclamations apply 30% less pressure.
theCloisteredRealm.note: Not built, both halves together: a proclamation's weight can be shifted by a flat figure and not by a share of itself.
deferred: cathedral towns keeping a rite learn and build far faster
and your proclamations press more gently for it
